chapter: New York, Philadelphia and Harlem nightlife
title: Café Society as America's first integrated nightclub
summary: He recalls prices, famous patrons and that Barney's club was integrated; Oscar Hammerstein served as host.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I showed Barney a menu a few days ago where back in 1946, something like that you could get a complete dinner for a dollar fifty cents. They had the standing there dollar and fifty cents/ like it had a halo. (Laughter).
And a dollar cover charge or something like that...
And we used to get a lot of people...Toscanini and... well, I don't know...was it Toscanini? Was he a conductor?

All those guys used to come in to hear Art Tatum. He had some people like Canada Lee. following. Paul Robeson...'cause Paul was, you know, he felt dejected. He used to come in...but those were very rare moments and they were moments that, when the final pages are written, it definitely will be part of the history. It will have to be.

I don't see how they can write...you know, I'm amazed at these guys writing...they don't even include all the names of the people who were there. I remember more names than they do. Zero Mostel, Jackie Gifford, Imogene Coca...they don't have them together with, you know what I mean. 'Cause Barney...
that was the first integrated night club in America. Did you know that?
Yeah. First integrated night club in America. Totally integrated. Imogene Coca and after her Art Tatum.

Audience, yeah. No problem to get in. All you had to do was try to make a reservation, because the damn thing was so popular, you know, that...You know, we had a man in Harlem at one time Oscar Hammerstein, was like an official host. When people were coming...say if Teddy Horne, Lena's father, or some person like that...the Jones boys from Chicago...if they were coming to New York they would phone Oscar and say, 'Listen, we'll be in town Thursday through Sunday. Plan, make plans for us.' What he would do would be to make reservations for the Café Society, and always ringside. Every place he took you, it was ringside. Wasn't no, you know what I mean, sitting behind a post or you didn't know..."Oh, Mr. Hammerstein, your party, right this way," you know, and he became quite an official host, you know, I mean like an official greeter for the city, you know. Especially with blacks, because some places were kind of funny, you know...sit you behind posts and all that shit...
